title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act s. 13 — Statutory provision (ACA s. 13)

content.overview: Section 13 establishes the procedural route for challenging an arbitrator on grounds agreed by the parties or on grounds falling within section 12. It preserves the arbitral process by requiring the challenge to be made before the tribunal in the manner and time prescribed.
content.glance: Section 13 establishes the procedural route for challenging an arbitrator on grounds agreed by the parties or on grounds falling within section 12. It preserves the arbitral process by requiring the challenge to be made before the tribunal in the manner and time prescribed.
content.study:
Section 13 — Challenge procedure

The parties are free to agree on a procedure for challenging an arbitrator, subject to the statutory framework. A party intending to challenge must send a written statement of the reasons for the challenge within the statutory period after becoming aware of the constitution of the tribunal or the circumstance forming the ground.

Unless the challenged arbitrator withdraws or the other party agrees to the challenge, the arbitral tribunal decides the challenge. If the challenge is unsuccessful, the tribunal continues the proceedings and makes the award. The statutory scheme then preserves the challenge as a ground in the later setting-aside framework rather than creating an ordinary immediate appeal against the tribunal's rejection.

examples.title: Application 1
examples.body: A party learns of a relevant relationship after appointment and submits a written challenge within the statutory period; the tribunal applies section 13 unless the challenged arbitrator withdraws or the other party agrees.

examples.title: Application 2
examples.body: An unsuccessful challenge does not by itself terminate the arbitration; the Act specifies the subsequent procedural consequence.
